# HarborSlate evening handoff

Shift coordinators at west-pier prepare a handoff so the next coordinator can see berth assignments and weather restrictions in the shift ticket. The terminal profile already selects west-pier. This page covers the evening handoff file and its attachment to that ticket.

## Produce the updated export

Use `hslate handoff export --shift evening --include-holds --out /var/tmp/evening-handoff.csv` for a handoff that includes weather holds. The new `--include-holds` flag adds weather-hold rows. The existing assignment rows are unchanged by this option, so the same ticket can still carry the berth information that coordinators expect.

## Close the handoff

Attach `/var/tmp/evening-handoff.csv` to the shift ticket before closing the handoff. Producing the file alone does not close anything. The next coordinator reads the ticket, so a file left only on the terminal is not the completed handoff.

## A line from an evening file

An example row is `weather_hold,F72,WX-9`. Read the columns in the order `record_type`, `sailing`, `reason_code`. F72 identifies the sailing, and WX-9 is the reason code supplied by Dispatch. Neither value names a berth. [Handoff columns](handoff-columns.md) is the supplemental field reference for interpreting the columns in the exported file.

## Berth policy

Berth allocation policy: Dispatch assigns berths. Shift coordinators may annotate a handoff but may not reassign a berth through this procedure.

## Begin the shift

Use an active shift-coordinator session before making an export. There is no terminal-selection command to add to the instructions for west-pier because the installed profile supplies that selection. The handoff workflow does not give coordinators authority to release Dispatch restrictions. Questions about a restriction go through [Dispatch contact](dispatch-contact.md).

## File background

The export is a local UTF-8 CSV. It is not delivered automatically. Without `--include-holds`, the export contains assignments only; include the flag when the handoff needs weather restrictions as well. A weather hold is a Dispatch restriction on a sailing, not a canceled sailing. A reader should therefore not use a weather-hold row as evidence that a sailing has been removed from the schedule.

## Terminal status

Run `hslate status --json` to inspect readiness. For an export using `--include-holds`, require `holds_synced` to be true before running the export. This field says that the local weather-hold ledger has caught up with Dispatch. It is not a statement about berth availability. If the field is false, wait for synchronization and check status again. Do not make a holds-inclusive export while it remains false. This procedure does not include a manual synchronization command.

## Reading row kinds

The `record_type` column identifies the kind of row. Its value `assignment` means a berth assignment, while `weather_hold` means a weather restriction. The combined file lets the next coordinator examine restrictions alongside assignments without treating the two row kinds as interchangeable. For a column-by-column description, use [Handoff columns](handoff-columns.md).
